<x_0.4863><y_0.4602>## CHAP. VI. OF THE SENSI<x_0.999><y_0.4898><class_Section-header>

<x_0.1807><y_0.5172>IN treating of the fenfes, we mean to confine ourfelves to the external ones of _touch_, _taffe_, _fmelling_, _bearing_, and _vijion_. The word _fenfe_, when applied to their five, feems to imply not only the fenfation ex cited in the mind by certain imprellions made on the body, but likewife the organ defined to receive and transmit thefe imprellions to the fenforium. Each of thefe organs being of a peculiar structure, is futeeptible only of particular imprellions, which will be pointed out as we proceed to deferibe each of them ferparately.<x_0.9785><y_0.7312><class_Text>

<x_0.1787><y_0.7789>THE fenfe of touch may be defined to be the faculty of diltinguithing certain properties of bodies by the feel. In a general acceptation, this definition might perhaps not improperly be extended to every part of the body potleefed of fenlibility (r), but it is commonly confined to the nervous papillae of the cutis, or true skin, which, with its appendages, and their several ufes, have been already defecribed.<x_0.9775><y_0.932><class_Text>
